concept.title: Password Reset Paths
concept.shortdesc: An overview of the two paths available for resetting a service desk agent's password, and when each applies.

conbody.p: There are two ways an agent's password can be reset: self-service, through the identity provider portal, and manual, through the identity management console by an administrator. Understanding when each path applies prevents unnecessary escalations to Tier 2 support.

Self-service is the default path and should be attempted first in nearly every case. It requires the agent to have access to their registered recovery email or authenticator app. Because it does not require administrator involvement, it is faster for the agent and does not consume support queue time.

The manual path exists specifically for cases where self-service is not possible — most commonly when an agent's recovery email account is itself inaccessible, or when an agent is newly onboarded and has not yet completed recovery-method setup. Because the manual path bypasses the agent's own verification step, it requires a secondary identity check performed by the administrator, as described in the related task topic.

Choosing the wrong path is a common source of delay: administrators sometimes default to the manual reset even when self-service would have worked, adding unnecessary steps and support-queue load. Confirming self-service availability first is part of the standard triage script.
